info.name: Agentcard Connect API
info.description: The Agentcard v2 API — connect your users and verify their identity from your own backend. Every call is authenticated with a platform access token minted from your `client_id` + `client_secret`.

request.description:
Sends a one-time code to the user by email or phone. Provide **exactly one** of `email` or `phone`. Codes are valid for 10 minutes.

If you've designed a connect email in your dashboard, we send that branded email; otherwise we send a default one.

response.name: The attempt. Pass its `id` back as `connect_id` when you verify.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `invalid_request` — missing or both of `email` and `phone`. `invalid_phone` — the number isn't valid or supported. `client_credentials_required` — the token wasn't minted from client credentials.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `unauthorized` — the platform access token is missing or expired. Exchange your client credentials for a fresh one.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `auth_provider_error` — the code couldn't be sent. Try again.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `auth_unavailable` — authentication is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.

request.description:
Checks the code the user entered and, on success, connects the user and returns the token pair to store. Completing the code **is** the authorization — there is no separate approval screen.

The returned `access_token` is the **user's connection token**: it acts on behalf of this user (send it as the bearer token to the MCP server to create cards, check balances, and shop as them). It is not the platform token — the endpoints in this reference keep using your platform access token and name the user with `user_id`.

A code can be verified once: a second verify of the same attempt returns `invalid_connect_attempt`.

In **sandbox** the code is always `111111`.

response.name: The connection. Store the token pair and `user.id` — every KYC call names the user by it.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `invalid_request` — missing `connect_id` or `code`. `invalid_connect_attempt` — the attempt is unknown, already used, or expired. `client_credentials_required` — the token wasn't minted from client credentials.

request.description:
Connection access tokens expire after one hour. Exchange the refresh token for a new pair before then.

Each refresh returns a **new** refresh token and invalidates the old one — replace the stored token every time.

response.name: The new token pair.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `invalid_request` — missing `refresh_token`. `client_credentials_required` — the token wasn't minted from client credentials.

header.description: Added as a part of security scheme: bearer

response.name: `invalid_refresh_token` — that refresh token is invalid or expired.

request.description: Ends your app's connection to a user. Every token your app holds for the user stops working, Vault session links they have not opened stop opening, and their cards stay in their Vault. Idempotent: a second call answers `200` with every count at `0`.

response.name: The user is disconnected from your app.
